Here's the reasoning:

The dependency chain T1 → T2 → T4 → T6 totals 2+2+3+3 = 10 days, exactly the full 10-day window, so this path has zero slack and must run back-to-back on one engineer. The other chain T1 → T3 → T5 (feeding into T6) totals 2+2+2 = 6 days and has slack, so it runs in parallel on the second engineer.

- E1 handles the critical path: T1 (days 1–2), T2 (days 3–4), T4 (days 5–7), T6 (days 8–10).
- E2 handles the parallel path: T3 (days 3–4, once T1 is done), T5 (days 5–6, once T3 is done), then is idle until the project ends (T6 needs both T4 and T5 done, and T4 finishes later on day 7, so T6 starts day 8).

All prerequisite and single-task-per-day constraints check out.
